findings.evidence: template/scripts/pr_review_gate.py reoffer(): the no-op early return is guarded by `action == "switch-provider" and state in pending and providers == previous`. A switch-provider on a blocked-retryable candidate with the same providers appends a new re-offer record and resets the unavailable streak. design.md says re-running with the providers already offered is a no-op without that restriction.
findings.summary: The spec says offering the providers already offered SHALL change nothing. The code applies that only to switch-provider on pending/reviewing/repairing states.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/pr_review_gate.py reoffer(): the blocked-retryable branch only requires adapter.retry_job_kind(candidate). It never checks that next_job is absent. Resuming a blocked-retryable candidate with a streak below 3 (which still has a retry-unavailable job) is accepted and replaces that job. The claim check still guards against a live claim, so the effect is benign, but it goes beyond the stated contract.
findings.summary: The spec scopes resume to blocked-retryable candidates without an automatic job. reoffer() does not check for one.
